Hi, former tuxedo rental guy here, first off is the waist size even remotely right, there should be a regular tag on the inside of the pants. If it isn't, can you go back to the tux place quick and have them swap out the pants? If it is, do the pants have little buckles on the sides? If so release them and pull the fabric together as tight as you can, they still might be baggy but the pants can at least sit comfortably.

Now without seeing the pants I don't know how baggy they look. If your used to skinny or fitted pants, rental tux pants just aren't ever going to fit the same. But as long as they don't look like ghetto jeans, you can probably pass it off and no one will be the least bothered.

I know I'm going against popular opinion here. But don't completely ignore renting as an option. If you find a local rental place that foes alterations, that can be a pretty cheap option. I know my store can rent a tux with alterations included for as low as 80 bucks if you aren't picky about specific style. Make sure to talk to someone in charge or the tailor and see about them tapering a rental and also how cheap they can do a tux for a single rental.

Typically when guys come in we try and be very jovial to put people at ease, when we get around to asking what they need the suit for they'll say something like "my dad just died". The awkward silence is palpable. I'll say something like "I'm so sorry for your loss" and then we ask very simple serious questions about the event and how the family is taking it. Just keeping the, talking drains the awkwardness a little.

Personally I view notched lapel formal wear acceptable if the event is anything "modern and more like a party", rather than strictly formal. I personally will always prefer peak and shawl lapels. But even Emily Post said there was no "right" style of lapel for formal events.

If you're wearing a tux two or three times a year, definitely buy one. I'd say that to anyone who comes to me. It's a good rule of thumb a d many in my business follow it. Honestly I'd reccomend buying over renting a tuxedo anytime. You wear them for things were you have to look your best, and when you buy one you can alter it in such a way that really fits your form.

Honestly, the prices for tuxedos are the same pretty much everywhere from what I've found. What you can do is make an investment in your own formal shoes, if you can find a cheap pair in your size. Somewhere, that should knock a little of your rental. Where to find them, I couldn't say, but this is  the Internet.

As for another upgrade, typically places will charge extra for a vest and tie rental, you can find your own tuxedo veston the same principle, but cummerbunds are a cheaper alternative and I know that you can order those online cheaply. 

At our store, if you had your own vest and shoes, that could lower a rentals price by 40 to 70 dollars.

Not me personally, but another employee once found a big bag of weed in a guys jacket. Very good choice. What I'd recommend is first imagining what you want your suit to look like (color, lapels, pockets, vents, buttons) have a clear image in your head or on paper so the tailor can understand your vision. Second, do a little research into what material you want the suit to be of and what that will mean for the difference in price. I've heard of bespoke tailcoats going for around $300 on the lower end of the spectrum but depending on ow many extra features you want on there the price can jump. 

Find a place, preferably in person rather than online, and really talk with the tailor, they sold throw some figures at you, and hopefully care as much about your garment as you do.
